summary: At segment 0 step 36, getpos.c:getpos() handles NHKF_GETPOS_MENU by toggling iflags.getloc_usemenu, printing the menu-mode message, and continuing the farlook loop. js/getpos.js:getpos() does not handle the configured getpos.menu key ('!'), so it falls through to the general command path. The resulting C message begins 'Using a menu to show possible targets…'; JavaScript enters the shell command instead. Port the missing whole branch and keep the cursor in getpos before the next input opens the monster target menu.

source.branch: getpos() handles NHKF_GETPOS_MENU by toggling iflags.getloc_usemenu, printing the enabled/disabled message, marking msg_given, and jumping to nxtc.
callers: cmd.c:doextcmd() can reach #name, and do_name.c:docallcmd() case 'm' calls getpos() for a selected monster; js/cmd.js calls js/getpos.js:getpos() through the matching map-location selection path.
dependencies: cmd.c initializes the NHKF_GETPOS_MENU key binding; js/command_bindings.js maps getpos.menu to '!'.
The existing getpos_menu() implementation in js/getpos.js handles the following target-menu selection once iflags.getloc_usemenu is enabled.
iflags.getloc_usemenu is the existing C state option exposed by the whatis_menu option and initialized false.

evidence: The saved v48 baseline evaluation identifies this case at segment 0 step 36 on key '!': C screen cell 'U' and JavaScript cell 'C'; both have the same RNG count through the divergence.

The documented single-case scan at replay commit 77e72da reports first mismatch at step 36 and cursor divergence at step 37, with the command sequence #wizgenesis, #wizmap, #name followed by the monster target menu interaction.

nethack-c/upstream/src/getpos.c:getpos() contains the NHKF_GETPOS_MENU branch that toggles getloc_usemenu, prints the mode message, marks msg_given, then goes to nxtc; js/getpos.js:getpos() has no corresponding branch although js/command_bindings.js maps getpos.menu to '!'.
